# Nxeon customer portal ("Nexion") — visual/interaction asset catalog for marketing-site reuse

Scope: read-only audit of `/opt/nxeon` (branch `main` as of 2026-09-27). Nothing in this repo
was edited, built, or deployed. All file paths below are absolute inside `/opt/nxeon`.

**Important prior art found during this audit**: `/opt/nxeon/app/newwebsitev4/` is an
existing, unpublished (`robots: noindex`) attempt at exactly this brief — a new marketing
page instructed to "match the button styling and visual language from the existing NXEON
customer portal... do not introduce a completely different button system." It already
demonstrates the correct pattern: portal CSS tokens/buttons copied verbatim into a scoped
`.v4` class in its own `v4.css` (not reusing the portal's `:has(.nx-shell-root)` block), and
one portal component (`RegionGlobe`) explicitly **forked** rather than imported, with a
code comment explaining exactly why ("every one of those changes landed in a component the
LIVE DEPLOY WIZARD renders on the money path... a marketing mock is not a good reason to put
risk into checkout"). Treat `app/newwebsitev4/v4.css` and `app/newwebsitev4/MarketingGlobe.tsx`
as a second, working reference alongside this document — they are literal proof the fork-not-import
approach works and roughly how much CSS it takes.

---

## 1. Design tokens

Source: `app/globals.css`, the block scoped to `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)` (line 244) is the
Nexion-only palette; the light-mode override lives at `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`
(line 316); `.nx-dark-island` (line 603) is the always-dark island scope. The bare `@theme`
block at the top of the file (line 8) is **production's original palette**, shared by
marketing/login/admin — do not confuse the two; they reuse the same variable *names*
(`--color-brand-500` etc.) with different values depending on which scope wins.

### Nexion-only colors (dark mode default — line 244-280)

| token | hex | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--color-brand-500` | `#8c3ae9` | Nexion violet, brand ramp midpoint (50→900 ramp defined) |
| `--color-navy-950` (page ground) | `#000816` | darkest — ground is deliberately darker than cards |
| `--color-navy-900` (card surface) | `#010f22` | |
| `--color-accent-blue` | `#2f7eef` | |
| `--color-accent-cyan` | `#14c5e4` | |
| `--color-cyan` | `#14c5e4` | Nexion-only name, never existed in production |
| `--color-blue` | `#2f7eef` | Nexion-only |
| `--color-violet` | `#8c3ae9` | Nexion-only |
| `--color-magenta` | `#d623e1` | Nexion-only |
| `--color-mint` | `#11c88e` | success |
| `--color-amber` | `#efa828` | warning |
| `--color-rose` | `#ef426c` | danger |
| `--color-neon-bug` | `#39ff6a` | bug-report button only |
| `--color-tx` / `-body` / `-mute` / `-dim` / `-faint` | `#fff` → `#5f7cb4` | text ramp, blue-tinted not neutral grey |
| `--color-rim` / `-soft` / `-hi` | `#002049` / `#00173b` / `#002a5e` | border/edge tokens, "zero-red blues" by design |
| `--radius-card` / `-nest` / `-chip` | `12px` / `8px` / `6px` | |

**The brand gradient** (blue → violet → magenta), exact stops used across the file:
- Deploy CTA / `.btn` background: `linear-gradient(110deg, #6f2ee0, #1a55cf, #2bb6d6, #6f2ee0)` (line 1666, 2005) — this is actually violet→blue→cyan→violet (a looping 4-stop gradient for the sliding-background trick), not a straight 3-stop.
- The "full brand sweep" CTA (`.nx-cta`, domains buy button, line 2905): `linear-gradient(100deg, #2f6fe0, #7b3fef 55%, #c33bea)` — this is the closest to a literal blue→violet→magenta 3-stop and is called out in-file as "distinct from `.btn-primary`... this is the 'buy' button."
- `.lgbtn` liquid-glass CTA edge (line 2384): `linear-gradient(100deg, #2f6fe8 0%, #7c3aed 52%, #c026d3 100%)` fill + a lighter `#7ff0ff → #b98cff → #ff90f6` edge gradient — very marketing-poster-worthy.
- The card-selected rim (`.card-on`, line 1944) and the liquid-glass card frame (`.lgc`, line 2408) both use a **conic-gradient** brand sweep (cyan → blue → violet → magenta → violet → cyan) rotating via the animated `--orbit` custom property — this is the "travelling rim" effect, one of the more distinctive assets (see §3).
- Region globe's ramp (`components/nx/RegionGlobe.tsx` line 34-38, and its marketing fork `app/newwebsitev4/MarketingGlobe.tsx`): `#3fbcd8 → #4f7cff → #d623e1`, explicitly commented "straight off the logo."
- Auth-card "chasing light" glow ring (`.glow-spin-a/-b`, line 936-1031): unscoped/shared already — blue→violet→cyan, ported from a sister product ("Kodely"). **This one is NOT Nexion-scoped and can be copied with zero token remapping.**

### Typography
`app/layout.tsx` (line 2, 13-14): **Geist** (sans) + **Geist Mono**, loaded via `next/font/google`,
exposed as CSS vars `--font-nx-sans` / `--font-nx-mono`, mapped in `globals.css` `@theme` to
Tailwind's `--font-sans` / `--font-mono`. Confirmed current (2026-09-14 comment: replaced an
older Plus Jakarta Sans / JetBrains Mono pairing). `app/newwebsitev4/layout.tsx` deliberately
reuses these two for body/mono text and adds a third display face (Archivo, weights 600/700)
only for hero-scale headlines — with an explicit comment rejecting Inter/Geist/Space Grotesk
as "a reliable tell of a generated page." Worth carrying that same reasoning into the new
marketing site.

### Shadows / glass / blur treatments
- `.card` (Nexion, line 1751): gradient border via double-background trick (`padding-box` fill
  + `border-box` gradient border), `box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,3,10,0.62), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(150,200,255,0.05)`, explicit `backdrop-filter: none` (see landmine below).
- `.glass` (Nexion "liquid glass", line 2318): `backdrop-filter: blur(24px) saturate(205%) brightness(1.05)`, three-layer effect: base blur+tint, `::before` lens-edge hairline gradient border, `::after` top-third gloss + `.glass-edge` a drifting highlight line. Extensively commented as "built from scratch against the concept, in the iOS-26 idiom."
- `.card-glass` (line 1783): a second, distinct glass treatment — no fill at all, pure `backdrop-filter: blur(24px) saturate(140%)`, with an L-shaped corner-hugging inner glow (`::before`, four edge-strip gradients blurred together) and a bright corner-accent ring (`::after`, mask-composite). Takes a per-instance `--tone` CSS var (default `#50b4ff`) so the same card can be recolored per page.
- `.glass-sm` (line 2358) / `.lgtile` (2368) — smaller-footprint versions of the same material for chips.

---

## 2. Buttons & controls

All in `app/globals.css`, mostly inside `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { @layer components { ... } }` starting at line 1557.

| class | location | what makes it distinctive |
|---|---|---|
| `.btn-primary` | 1602-1663 | "Candidate C3" — flat dark gradient face (`linear-gradient(180deg,#101B36,#0B1225)`), a static hairline gradient rim via double-pseudo-element mask trick, and on **hover** a brighter conic-gradient arc (`--nx-btn-spin`, animated `@property`) sweeps one full lap around the rim (`btn-primary-spin`, 1.15s). Lifts 1px on hover. |
| `.btn-deploy` / `.btn` | 1664-2080 (two near-duplicate definitions — production's `.btn-deploy` at 1074 and Nexion's `.btn` at 2000 share the same mechanism) | Pill shape, 4-stop looping gradient background (`background-size:220%`) that slides across on hover, PLUS a one-shot diagonal shine/shimmer sweep (`::before`, `btn-sweep`/`btn-deploy-sweep` keyframes, skewed white gradient translating across), a 1px lift, and an arrow (`.arw`/`.dep-arrow`) that nudges 3px right on hover. This is probably the single most "premium SaaS CTA" button in the set. |
| `.btn-pay` | 2063 | Modifier on `.btn` — same motion, cyan→pink gradient instead of violet/blue, used only for the one control that takes money. |
| `.nx-cta` | 2902 | The domains/"buy" gradient CTA, blue→violet→magenta, simpler (no sweep), `filter:brightness(1.08)` on hover, press state translates 1px down. |
| `.lgbtn` | 2378 | Liquid-glass CTA: dark fill + a light gradient border (double-background layering) + a genuine directional bloom (`box-shadow` with off-axis cyan-left/magenta-right glows) that intensifies on hover. Very screenshot-worthy. |
| `.btn-secondary` / `.btn-ghost` / `.btn-danger` | 1672-1692 | Simple bordered/tinted variants, no special motion. |
| `.chip` / `.chip-on` | 2093-2134 | Pill filter chip; selected state drops the pill entirely and just glows the text (`text-shadow`), with a light-mode override using an underline instead (glow reads badly on white). |
| `.chip-tone` (+ `.chip-amber/-violet/-mint/-blue/-slate/-rose`) | 2170-2188 | HSL-driven single-hue chip (fill/border/icon/text all one hue family) — parameterized via `--chip-h/-s/-hm` custom properties rather than six hand-mixed hex sets. Clean pattern to copy for a marketing "role/status" pill. |
| `.badge` (+ `-mint/-amber/-rose/-cyan`) | 2137-2150 | Solid gradient-filled pill, glow shadow. |
| `.nx-tab` / `.nx-tab-on` | 2561-2593 | Underlined text tab: active tab gets a `linear-gradient(#5fd0ff,#8c3ae9,#ff6fd8)` underline with a glow; **hover** on an inactive tab scales the same gradient bar in from the left (`transform:scaleX`) rather than fading — reads as "a loading bar filling." |
| `.nxsel` | 2028 | Themed native `<select>` — needed because the OS-painted option list forces its own dark background (`.nxsel > option`). |
| `.nx-range` / `.range` | 2264-2792 | Custom-styled range slider — gradient-filled track up to the thumb, glowing white thumb with a colored ring. |
| `.field-bad` | 2043 | Validation error state — red border/ring **plus** a `nx-shake` keyframe (re-triggered on every failed submit via React key) so movement, not just color, draws the eye. |
| `.nx-settings input[type=checkbox]` | 2539 | A from-scratch toggle switch (no native checkbox visible), gradient fill when checked, sliding thumb. |
| `.promo-bar` / `.promo-copy-btn` etc. | 3005-3372 | The whole trial-promo popup/bar system — see §3, it's **unscoped** (works outside the portal already, tokens-based). |

---

## 3. Hover & motion effects

All `@keyframes` in `app/globals.css`, grouped by where they're declared (bare `@theme` block =
shared/production-original; the `@layer components` block right after the portal scope header
at line 1418 = Nexion-only, deliberately hoisted **outside** the `:has()` wrapper — see the CSS
landmine note below on why).

**Shared/production keyframes** (bare `@theme`, lines 99-214): `bell-shake`, `price-pop`,
`panel-in`/`panel-out`, `gh-pop`, `grow-up`, `grow-x`, `eq` (audio-equalizer bars), `blink`
(terminal cursor), `sweep` (soft light sweep), `line-in`, `orbit-spin`, `check-pop`/`check-draw`
(SVG stroke-draw checkmark), `ring-glow`. These already work anywhere (no `.nx-shell-root`
needed) — copy freely.

**Nexion-only keyframes** (hoisted @layer block, lines 1426-1555): `btn-primary-spin` (uses
`@property --nx-btn-spin`), `nx-breathe` (slow float+scale for hero art), `btn-sweep`,
`nx-shake`, `nx-float`, `nx-spin`, `nx-ring` (expanding fading ring, used for provisioning),
`nx-pop` (bouncy scale-in, `cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1)`), `nx-sheen`, `nx-rise`,
**`nx-levitate` / `nx-levitate-shadow`** (the hero rack's weightless hover — the rack rises/falls
6.5s while its cast shadow breathes opposite it, see `RackHero.tsx` + the CLAUDE.md landmine
about this exact animation freezing once already), `caret`, `dot-ring`/`dot-breathe` (live
status-dot pulse+ring), `nx-card-in`, the whole **preloader set** (`nx-pre-spin`, `nx-pre-slab`,
`nx-pre-halo`, `nx-pre-bar`), `nxp-ping`/`nxp-sheen`/`nxp-fade`/`nxp-in`/`nxp-trace` (VPS panel
modal/skeleton motion), `nx-tag-pulse-dot`/`-bleed`, `nx-mic-pulse`, `nx-typing-bounce`
(3-dot chat "is typing" indicator), `nx-mig-spin` (migration ring sweep, `@property`-driven),
`nx-res-in`, `nx-msg-in` (chat bubble entrance).

**Notable named effects and where they live:**
- **The page preloader** — `components/nx/Preloader.tsx` + CSS lines 2637-2695. CSS-only
  (deliberately, since it renders before the page's own JS is ready): the real Logo's three
  slabs redrawn as separate SVG `<path>`s that light in sequence, a conic-gradient arc sweep
  masked to a hairline ring (`nx-pre-ring`), a breathing halo (`nx-pre-halo`), and an
  indeterminate scanning bar (`nx-pre-bar`). Extremely portable — pure CSS + inline SVG, one
  React component, no backend or portal scoping dependency at all beyond `--color-*` tokens
  and the `Icon` import (which the marketing copy would drop, since the SVG is inlined).
- **The provisioning/deploy animation** — `components/nx/Provisioning.tsx` (467 lines). This
  is the "server is being built" screen: a held-up product icon (`SvcIcon`) floating
  (`nx-float`) with two staggered expanding rings (`nx-ring`), a real (not simulated) stepper
  list with per-stage spinners/checkmarks, and a `.bar` progress fill with a traveling sheen
  (`nx-sheen`). **This is explicitly wired to real backend progress** (`liveStep` from
  `Server.provisioningStep`) with a `simulate` prop that only fires in sandbox mode — for a
  marketing "product showcase" mock this would need to be forked and hardcoded to `simulate`-
  style fake progression (same pattern `MarketingGlobe.tsx` already used for the globe).
  Visually this is one of the strongest "premium SaaS" set-pieces in the whole product.
- **The travelling conic-gradient rim** — `.card-on` (line 1939) and `.lgc` (line 2406) both
  animate `@property --orbit` (declared top-of-file, line 5) via `lgc-orbit` (6-9s linear) to
  spin a conic-gradient painted into a `border-box` under a solid `padding-box` fill — this is
  how the "selected plan card" and the liquid-glass card frame get a genuinely rotating
  rainbow-brand edge with clean rounded corners (a `border-image` cannot round corners; this
  can). Good marketing-page "featured/highlighted" card treatment.
- **Aurora / ambient backgrounds** — several independent implementations, not one shared
  system: `AuroraBg.tsx` (canvas, layered drifting ribbons, capped 30fps, additive blend in
  dark mode / normal blend + darker palette in light mode), `RackHero.tsx` (canvas, two-layer
  "in front of / behind the rack" filament bundles, cyan→magenta), `StreamsBg.tsx`,
  `PlateBg.tsx`, `BlobField.tsx`, `Ribbons.tsx`, plus **per-page aurora components**
  (`BillingAurora`, `DomainsAurora`, `PartnerAurora`, `SettingsAurora`, `TeamAurora`,
  `SupportAurora`, `MailAurora`, `SslAurora`, `ServicesAurora`, `ToolsAurora`,
  `WhatsNewAurora`, `FeedbackAurora`) — each a bespoke canvas/CSS treatment for one dashboard

### CSS landmines to respect when copying (from CLAUDE.md, all directly relevant here)

1. **`@keyframes` / `@property` cannot be nested inside a plain style rule** (only inside
   `@layer`/`@media`/top level). The Nexion CSS itself already got bitten by this once — note
   the block at globals.css line 1418-1556 titled "Hoisted out of `:root:has(...)`", which
   exists *because* nesting those keyframes inside the has-scope silently killed ~34
   animations. When copying any Nexion keyframe into a marketing stylesheet, keep it at the
   top level (or inside `@layer`/`@media`), never nested inside a class selector.
2. **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed`
   descendants.** `.card` explicitly cancels an inherited `backdrop-filter: none` for exactly
   this reason (globals.css line 1580). Any marketing modal/overlay nested inside a copied
   `.glass`/`.card` needs the same care, or `createPortal` to `document.body`.
3. A **fixed, `z-0` decorative background** (aurora/globe) must sit behind real content that
   has `relative z-[1]`, or it paints on top. All the aurora components in `components/nx/`
   already follow this pattern (`pointer-events-none`, `z-0`, faded into the page background
   via a gradient overlay div) — copy that structure, not just the canvas.
4. Percentage `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item with no defined container
   dimension silently no-ops — give any ported hero/aurora wrapper a real `inset-0`/fixed
   height rather than relying on percentage insets alone.
5. `.card-on`/`.glow-*`/etc. reference custom properties (`--orbit`, `--nx-btn-spin`,
   `--nx-mig-spin`) that must be registered via `@property` at a valid top level — verify these
   ship along with any button/card copy, not just the visible box-shadow/gradient rules.

## 6. Portability notes

**General rule confirmed by `app/newwebsitev4`:** copy CSS blocks and components into the
marketing codebase under new names/scopes; never import `components/nx/*` directly into a
marketing route, and never write a bare (unscoped) rule for a class name the portal or
production also uses (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.glass`, `.input`, etc.) — that is the exact
bug class CLAUDE.md documents at length (the `:has(.nx-shell-root)` scoping mechanism exists
*because* an earlier, unscoped version of this exact palette leaked into marketing/login/admin
site-wide). If the new marketing site is a separate codebase entirely, this is moot; if it's
built as another route inside `/opt/nxeon` (as `newwebsitev4` was), it is the single most
important rule to follow.

| Owner's premium PNG art | `public/nx/art/*.webp` (+ PNG masters) | None — static assets, owner-licensed per the README | **Trivial.** Just copy the `.webp` files. Best ROI item in this whole audit. |
| Logo/brand marks | `components/nx/Logo.tsx`, `public/nx-mark.png`, `public/logo.png` | None | **Trivial** — these are literally the same files the marketing site's *current* header already uses, so there is nothing to port at all, just reference them. |

### CSS landmines to respect when copying (from CLAUDE.md, all directly relevant here)

1. **`@keyframes` / `@property` cannot be nested inside a plain style rule** (only inside
   `@layer`/`@media`/top level). The Nexion CSS itself already got bitten by this once — note
   the block at globals.css line 1418-1556 titled "Hoisted out of `:root:has(...)`", which
   exists *because* nesting those keyframes inside the has-scope silently killed ~34
   animations. When copying any Nexion keyframe into a marketing stylesheet, keep it at the
   top level (or inside `@layer`/`@media`), never nested inside a class selector.
2. **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed`
   descendants.** `.card` explicitly cancels an inherited `backdrop-filter: none` for exactly
   this reason (globals.css line 1580). Any marketing modal/overlay nested inside a copied
   `.glass`/`.card` needs the same care, or `createPortal` to `document.body`.

   has `relative z-[1]`, or it paints on top. All the aurora components in `components/nx/`
   already follow this pattern (`pointer-events-none`, `z-0`, faded into the page background
   via a gradient overlay div) — copy that structure, not just the canvas.
4. Percentage `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item with no defined container
   dimension silently no-ops — give any ported hero/aurora wrapper a real `inset-0`/fixed
   height rather than relying on percentage insets alone.

   `--nx-mig-spin`) that must be registered via `@property` at a valid top level — verify these
   ship along with any button/card copy, not just the visible box-shadow/gradient rules.

   most "SaaS premium" button in the product: sliding gradient + shimmer sweep + arrow nudge.

   else in the codebase.

   visual most competitor hosting sites don't have.
6. **Liquid-glass card system** (`.glass`, `.card-glass`, `GlassFilters.tsx`) — distinctive
   "iOS-26 idiom" material, good for feature cards or a pricing table.
7. **The rotating conic-gradient card rim** (`.card-on`/`.lgc`, driven by `@property --orbit`)
   — an eye-catching "featured plan" treatment for a pricing page.
8. **`RackHero.tsx`** — the aurora-wrapped server rack; strong hero-section candidate, check
   if `newwebsitev4` already uses it before rebuilding.
9. **Promo popup/carousel** (`PromoCarousel.tsx` + `.promo-*`) — already unscoped/portable,
   real working conversion tool (countdown, coupon box, poster collage), not just decoration.
10. **Icon system** (133 vector icons + neon glow via `.nx-ico`) — consistent, on-brand, easy
    to drop into any marketing layout needing feature-list icons.
11. **`.nx-cta` / `.lgbtn`** — the full blue→violet→magenta brand-sweep buttons, good for a
    single standout "Get started" CTA distinct from ordinary buttons.
12. **`Stepper.tsx`** — clean responsive step indicator, reusable for an onboarding/signup
    flow walkthrough on the marketing site.
13. **`.lg-stage`/`.lg-tilt` pointer-following 3D card** — a tilting, cast-shadow "object"
    treatment that would make a great interactive hero product shot.
14. **`Sparkline`/`AreaChart`/`Donut` (charts.tsx)** — real, dependency-free SVG charts for a
    "here's your dashboard" marketing screenshot, fed with sample data.
15. **Status dot (`.dot-live`)** — small but very "alive"-feeling detail (breathing glow +
    expanding ring) — good for a "servers online now" style live-status widget.
16. **`.nx-tab` hover-fill-bar tabs** — a small but genuinely nice interaction detail for any
    marketing page with a tabbed feature comparison.
17. **`nx-levitate` hero-float animation** — subtle, considered motion (6.5s, shadow breathing
    opposite the object) rather than a generic bounce; good for any floating hero graphic.
18. **`.card-glass` corner-glow treatment** — distinctive enough to be recognizable as "Nxeon"
    without being loud; good for supporting feature cards below a hero.
19. **`.badge`/`.chip-tone` HSL-parameterized status pills** — clean, consistent, easy to
    extend with new brand colors for marketing use (e.g. "New", "Popular", "Beta" tags).
20. **The auth-card "chasing light" glow ring** (`.glow-clip-a/-b`, unscoped already) — free to
    use with zero remapping since it's not inside the portal's `:has()` scope at all.
21. **Real game art/logos** (`public/games/art/*.jpg`, `public/logos/games/*.png`) — for any
    "supported games" marketing grid, prefer these over `GameArt.tsx`'s procedural fallback.
22. **`.field-bad` shake + glow validation state** — a small, well-considered form-error detail
    worth copying wholesale for any marketing lead-gen form.
23. **`.nxp-skel` shimmer skeleton** — nicer loading placeholder than the plain `.skeleton`,
    good if the marketing "product preview" needs to fake a loading state.
24. **Wordmark lockup** (`/logo.png`, `components/nx/Logo.tsx`'s `Wordmark`) — already the

    canonical logo file to keep using.
